A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Diagonal Flow Matching research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across additions, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original model comparisons on gas turbine, Unifoil, and DTLZ datasets, plus permutation, diversity, and uncertainty-quantification experiments in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds thin-film and FashionMNIST experiments, surrogate and solver robustness checks, and additional OOD evaluations.

M1.justification: The zero-anchored states, flow-matching objective, and uncertainty algorithms remain unchanged. V2 adds a task-specific architectural extension for FashionMNIST: a U-Net-style CNN with skip connections, FiLM conditioning, and bottleneck self-attention that predicts image and label velocities (Appendix F.7). V1 used MLP velocity networks.

E1.justification: V2 adds thin-film optical coating with 128 layer thicknesses and 64 reflectance labels, and FashionMNIST inverse generation from five image statistics with 784 pixel variables. It also adds Unifoil tests involving negative drag, extreme lift-to-drag ratios, below-polar targets, and shifted Mach/angle-of-attack conditions. The original three datasets remain.

E2.justification: The benchmark comparator set remains standard CFM and INN, including on the added datasets. Retained UQ comparisons continue to evaluate Ensemble Variance and FM Loss, with random/oracle references where applicable. The added simulation-based-inference citation is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Existing experimental settings are retained, while substantial new protocols are added. These include 50,000/10,000/10,000 training/validation/test splits, label normalization, generated-output clamping, and benchmark-specific architectures and training schedules. Appendices D, E, and H additionally specify surrogate perturbations, nine ODE solver configurations, OOD distance bands, and physical OOD tests using 1,000 in-distribution and 1,000 OOD samples.

E4.justification: New Appendix D tests sensitivity to surrogate-output noise and nine independently trained Unifoil evaluators. Appendix E tests Euler, RK4, and adaptive Dopri5 integration. Appendix H adds OOD-distance sweeps and physical/conditioning-shift stress tests. These substantially expand the robustness evidence beyond v1's retained permutation, accuracy-conditioned diversity, and original OOD analyses.

E5.justification: The original five-run reporting practice remains. New Table 8 specifies averaging over five noise seeds and reports means and ranges across nine Unifoil surrogates trained using three architectures and three seeds each. These add variability estimation for the robustness experiments without establishing an increased run count for the original experiments.

E6.justification: Original result-table entries are retained. New Tables 4 and 5 report Diag-CFM round-trip errors of 2.247e-2 on thin films and 9.15e-3 on FashionMNIST, lowest among the three methods in each setting. Further tables add surrogate, solver, and OOD findings. The select-best improvement range is corrected from 13–31% to 5–31%, and Zero-Deviation rejection improvement from 10–27% to 8–27%, matching existing tables. New Table 13 reports gas-turbine hard-OOD AUC 0.773, while retained Figure 8 shows 0.754; this discrepancy is unexplained.

T1.justification: Propositions 4.1–4.2 and their Appendix A proofs are unchanged. Appendices C.4–C.5 add mathematical specifications of the new forward problems, including layer transfer matrices and the five image-statistic functions in Table 7. This is a limited addition of formal definitions, without new theoretical guarantees.

C1.justification: The central zero-anchoring, permutation-invariance, and uncertainty-metric contributions remain. Their stated validation scope expands from three tasks and P=100 to five tasks and P=784. The abstract limits order-of-magnitude gains to several benchmarks, and the conclusion replaces the earlier across-all-datasets order-of-magnitude claim with substantially improved accuracy.

C2.justification: V2 narrows the high-dimensional forward-prediction limitation specifically to DTLZ, arguing from the added benchmarks that it is not a generic dimensionality failure. It also interprets surrogate and solver robustness as supporting the reliability of the reported rankings and Zero-Deviation signal, and explains detection of infeasible lift/drag combinations despite individually in-range labels.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-access statement for a reference implementation with runnable DTLZ2, thin-film, and FashionMNIST examples. Appendices C and F substantially expand technical documentation with new forward-map definitions, splits, preprocessing, CNN/MLP configurations, and training schedules; Appendices D–E specify robustness procedures. The code-access claim is documented in the PDF, without external verification.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds Wildberger et al. on flow matching for simulation-based inference and distinguishes conditional posterior sampling from the paper's bidirectional mapping. New citations to Luce, Ma, and Xiao support the added benchmarks. Most research positioning remains unchanged; consolidation of Lipman's preprint and publication references does not remove a distinct prior work.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained. V2 inserts two experimental subsections and two robustness appendices, updates cross-references and appendix labels, adds code availability and acknowledgements, and makes localized abstract, conclusion, bibliographic, and publication-footer edits.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the tabular presentation with benchmark Tables 4–5, mathematical-definition Table 7, surrogate/solver Tables 8–9, and OOD Tables 13–14. The original Figures 1–10 and earlier result tables are retained, with changed placement and table numbering. The general main-text and appendix layout styles remain.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation missing in v1: surrogate and solver checks directly probe dependence on evaluation approximations, while physically motivated OOD tests and two exact-forward benchmarks strengthen evidence for reliability and broader applicability. Added technical documentation and code-access information improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses: the gas-turbine AUC discrepancy between Table 13 and Figure 8 remains unexplained, and Table 14 includes an ensemble win despite retained blanket UQ-superiority claims.
